<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par145 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=3}} (according to the accents); 22:23, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=וּבֹסֶר גֹּמֵל יִֽהְיֶה נִצָּה|translate=and a ripening grape the flower becometh}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|r}}
(''b'') The adjective in a noun-clause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=137}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשָׁר מִשְׁפָּטֶ֫יךָ|translate=upright are thy judgements}}; cf. verse 155.<ref>This does not include such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=7}}, 10, where {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹם}} is rather to be explained as an accusative denoting a state, {{GHGpar|118|n}}.</ref>—On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=רֹעֵה}} in {{GHGheb|text=רֹעֵה צֹאן עֲבָדֶ֫יךָ|translate=thy servants are shepherds}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=3}}, is either an unusual orthography or simply a misspelling for {{GHGheb|text=רֹעֵי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|s}}
Rem. 1. As soon as a sentence which begins with an uninflected predicate is carried on after the mention of the subject, the gender and number of the subsequent (co-ordinate) predicates must coincide with those of the subject, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי מְאֹרֹת... וְהָיוּ}} (see o above); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=1}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=39}} (see p above).

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|t}}
2. The dislike mentioned in ''p'' above, of using the feminine form (cf., further, {{GHGpar|144|a}}, with the sections of the Grammar referred to there, and below, under ''u''), is exemplified sometimes by the fact that of several predicates only that which stands next to the feminine substantive is inflected as feminine (cf. the treatment of several attributes following a feminine substantive, {{GHGpar|132|d}}); thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=רָֽגְזָה}}, and afterwards {{GHGheb|text=עוֹרֵר}} (but {{GHGheb|text=עוֹרֵר}} is better taken as an infin. abs.=''excitando'', reading {{GHGheb|text=הָקֵם}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}}); 33:9 {{GHGheb|text=אָבַל אֻמְלְלָה אֶ֫רֶץ|translate=mourneth, languisheth the land}}. Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=19}}, and the examples ({{GHGpar|47|k}}) where only the first of several consecutive forms of the 2nd sing. fem. imperf. has the afformative ''î'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=32|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=תִּֽהְיֶה}} after {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁתִּי}}); on the converse sequence of genders in imperatives, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=15}}, cf. {{GHGpar|110|k}}.—Of a different kind are instances like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=2|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, where {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=person}} (fem.) as the narrative continues, assumes (in agreement with the context) the sense of a masculine person.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|u}}
3. The instances in which the gender or number of the ''following'' predicate appears to differ from that of the subject are due partly to manifest errors in the text, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=9}} read with the Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֶחָד}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאַחַת}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}} then follows correctly; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=20}} read with Wellhausen {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאֻל}}, according to 1:28, instead of {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאַל}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=4}} read {{GHGheb|text=וַיּֽאֹמְרוּ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=29}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=יִתָּכֵן}} read the plural as in verse 25; so also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=38}} for {{GHGheb|text=יָבוֹא}},
<ref>{{GHGheb|text=יבוא}} probably an error for {{GHGheb|text=יבאו}}. The Masora on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=34}} reckons fourteen instances of {{GHGheb|text=יָבֹא}}, where we should expect the plural.</ref> and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=20}} for {{GHGheb|text=נָּטָ֑ח}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=5|verse=10}} read {{GHGheb|text=נִכְמָר}}, and cf. in general, {{GHGpar|7|d}}, note; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=2|verse=48}} read {{GHGheb|text=יָלְֽדָה}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=15}} also the text is certainly corrupt. Other instances are due to special reasons. The anomalies in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=16}} (after {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלָיו}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=11|verse=4}} (after {{GHGheb|text=עֵינָיו}}), 63:4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, 32 18:6, 26:23, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=6}} (all after {{GHGheb|text=שְׂפָתַ֫יִם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=2}} (after {{GHGheb|text=מִצְוֹתַי}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=22}} (after {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנוֹת}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=41}} (read {{GHGheb|text=וְרִבּוּת}}), and perhaps {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=17}} are also to be explained (see p) from the dislike of the 3rd plur. fem. imperf.; moreover, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=23}} the plur. masc. even of a participle occurs instead of the plur. fem.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=8}} f. {{GHGheb|text=יִהְֽיֶה}}, after a plural subject, is explained as a case of attraction to the following singular predicate.<ref>So also the pronoun {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} emphatically resuming the subject (see {{GHGpar|141|h}}) is attracted to the predicate in number in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=13|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=אִשֵּׁי יְהֹוָה... הוּא נַֽחֲלָתוֹ|translate=the offerings of the Lord... that is his inheritance}}; in number and gender, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=33}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=3}}.</ref>—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=רֹבֵץ}}<section end=par145 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
